metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in North Washington, CO | DJ Basin
metaDescription: Own severed minerals under North Washington, CO subdivisions? We check the Adams County DJ Basin flank and setback limits before quoting your interest.
heroLead: North Washington is a small unincorporated Adams County community wedged into the north Denver metro area, where farmland turned into housing decades ago while mineral rights often stayed with the original owning family.
intro: If you hold minerals here, they were almost certainly severed from the surface generations back, when this stretch north of Denver was still agricultural rather than suburban. That history matters because it means most North Washington-area interests today are either tied to older, established wells or sit entirely undrilled beneath dense residential development.

sections.heading: Metro Denver drilling constraints
paragraphs: New well siting this close to Denver's urban core faces real practical and regulatory limits, especially since SB 19-181 gave local governments stronger authority to set setback and permitting standards around homes and schools in 2019. Existing wells that predate current housing generally continue producing under the rules in place when permitted, but new development on undrilled acreage is much less likely here than in open Weld County ground.
That makes it especially important to establish, before anything else, whether your North Washington interest has ever actually produced.

sections.heading: How we evaluate it
paragraphs: We check COGCC records for any well history tied to your legal description and review applicable Adams County land-use rules. If there's an active well, we quote against its real production; if not, we price the acreage as speculative and tell you so directly.

faqs.question: Is there any drilling activity near North Washington today?
faqs.answer: Very limited given the dense residential development. We check whether an established well already exists on your section before assuming either way.

faqs.question: How did my family end up owning minerals under someone else's house?
faqs.answer: Common pattern across the Denver metro's DJ Basin fringe — the surface was farmland sold decades ago, with mineral rights kept separate by the original family.

faqs.question: Is undeveloped acreage here worth anything?
faqs.answer: Potentially, though priced as speculative long-term value rather than an income stream, since active development this close to the city is limited.

faqs.question: What paperwork should I gather before contacting you?
faqs.answer: Any deed, will, or probate document that shows how you came to own the mineral interest, plus your legal description if you have it. We can help fill in gaps from there.

faqs.question: Does it matter that North Washington is unincorporated?
faqs.answer: Not for the mineral evaluation itself. We work from the legal description and applicable county records rather than any particular municipal designation.
